title: Practical: Contact Manager
story: Your phone has 200 contacts and scrolling is a nightmare. You decide to build a smarter contact manager: search by name instantly (Map), show all contacts alphabetically (Vec of names), and add new contacts without duplicates (Set for uniqueness checking).
why: A real-world app combining Map for fast lookup and Vec for ordered display — this pattern appears in almost every application that manages records.
analogy: A contact manager with Map + Vec is like a phone book with both an index (Map) and page-by-page listings (Vec). The index lets you jump straight to 'Smith, John' instantly. The page-by-page listing lets you browse everyone in order. Both views of the same data, each serving a different purpose.
try_it: Add an email field by making the Map value a struct with phone and email. Add a `remove_contact` function that removes from both the Map and the Vec. Add a `search` function that finds all contacts whose names contain a substring (loop through names Vec, check with string.contains).
tips: Maintain both collections in sync — every add/remove must update both the Map and the Vec
Use Map for O(1) lookup by name, Vec for ordered iteration and display
Extract repetitive patterns into helper functions (`add_contact`, `remove_contact`) to avoid bugs
common_mistakes: Updating one collection but not the other — the Map and Vec get out of sync and show different data
Using the Vec to find a contact — scanning a 200-item Vec when Map.get() is instant
Forgetting that removing from the middle of a Vec is expensive — if you remove contacts often, consider a different approach
